summary: High-level discovery: Novagrid evaluating Redwood for customer-facing generative features. Primary questions: hosted vs dedicated vs private, open model tradeoffs (context length, multilingual, tool-calling), throughput/latency targets and security (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, run multilingual perf benchmark and schedule deep-dive.
topics: model selection: open models vs curated variants
context length and long-form support (16k+ tokens)
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ruiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood. Marcus, our SE, is with me. Quick intros?
[00:08] Ananya Patel: Hi, I'm Ananya, Head of ML at Novagrid. We own the recommendation and generative pipelines.
[00:12] Tom Eriksen: Tom, platform eng, infra owner.
[00:14] Lena Zhou: Lena, security and compliance.
[00:16] Marcus Lee: Marcus, solutions engineer, focus on model serving and perf. Happy to dive in.
[00:20] Sofia: Cool. Today high level figure out model selection needs: open models, context length, multilingual, and if tool-calling is required. We'll also cover hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:30] Ananya: Great. To start, our use case: customer-facing assistant that can do long-form summary generation from multi-doc inputs (support tickets, knowledge base), plus multi-lingual prompt answering for EMEA and APAC. Latency target is sub-1s per inference for short queries, and for long-form batching we care more about throughput.
[00:48] Marcus: Got it. When you say multi-doc, what's the typical sequence length?
[00:52] Ananya: Usually 8k tokens, sometimes up to 20k when we bundle several docs and chat history. We want to explore context windows 16k and 32k.
[00:58] Sofia: OK so longer context models are important. On Redwood's side we support a model catalog with verified performance profiles and longer context variants; we also do kv caching for repeated prefixes — sorry, "K V cash" in the transcripts sometimes, uh, KV cache. That reduces cost for chat scenarios.
[01:15] Tom: Question on hosted vs dedicated: if we go hosted, are we able to pin a model version and get consistent latency? We don't want noisy neighbor effects.
[01:23] Marcus: Yes you can pin model versions in hosted. For strict SLAs and predictable throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity). Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools and predictable throughput. For the most strict data residency and isolation requirements we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).
[01:35] Lena: We will need SOC2 and ISO docs, and support for our KMS. Also SSO (SAML) and RBAC.
[01:41] Sofia: We'll share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs after the call. Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[01:47] Ananya: Back to models — what are the open models you typically recommend for high-quality multilingual and long context? We've looked at Mistral, Llama-3 variants, MPT, and some of the 70B open models.
[01:58] Marcus: Right now the common pattern: for short queries lower-latency usage you can use trimmed, faster variants, e.g., quantized Llama-3-70B non-8-bit (we call them curated variants). For long context we recommend models trained or compiled with long-context support — some chains have 32k context. We also have Redwood-verified variants optimized by compilation and kernel choices.
[02:18] Ananya: How about multilingual quality? We need solid performance in Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean.
[02:24] Marcus: Mistral & Llama-3-70B mixed language variants perform well; Mistral tends to be strong on code and English, M-Llama variants or fine-tuned multilingual Llama-3 often give better non-English BLEU/accuracy. We'll propose a shortlist with expected per-lang benchmarks.
[02:37] Tom: Are there big differences in token cost between these models? We care about unit economics.
[02:41] Sofia: Yes; model size and quantization level drive cost. Hosted per-token pricing varies by model family; dedicated gives you lower unit cost for reserved capacity. Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quantization profiles to reduce unit cost while keeping quality targets. We'll send cost comparisons.
[02:56] Ananya: Tool-calling — our assistant must call internal tools: ticket search, billing lookup. Do models need special support for tool-calling/function calling?
[03:03] Marcus: We support structured tool calling and function-calling semantics. Some open models handle function call prompting better out-of-the-box; others need a lightweight orchestration layer. Redwood's runtime supports tool hooks and you can configure safe fallbacks. We also have structured output helpers.
[03:20] Lena: On security, if we use hosted, is customer data stored? Can we disable retention?
[03:25] Sofia: Hosted has configurable retention — default short retention for logs and you can opt out. Dedicated and Private give stronger isolation and you can manage retention policies. We'll include the retention options doc.
[03:35] Ananya: For benchmarking, we'd like to run a multilingual perf+quality pass across 5 model families with our 1k prompts, want to measure latency, tokens/s, and per-lang accuracy. Can Redwood run that or do we need to run it ourselves?
[03:47] Marcus: We can run a Redwood-hosted benchmark against our catalog (sanitized data) or you can provide dataset and we run it within a private tenant for realistic numbers. For strict data residency we can run the bench on Dedicated or Private.
[03:59] Tom: In terms of throughput, if we do long-form generation — e.g., 20k tokens — what are realistic latencies?
[04:05] Marcus: For long generative workflows latency scales with tokens and GPU type. On A100-class hardware you'll see better throughput; our runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache to improve effective latency for chat patterns. For 20k tokens it's more of a minutes scale for full generation but per-token speed is optimized. We'll provide example numbers per GPU.
[04:24] Ananya: One gotcha: we will need multilingual context windows — maintain history across languages as well — and some prompts will call tools mid-conversation. We also need deterministic outputs for certain billing reconciliations.
[04:34] Marcus: Determinism is tricky; you can control sampling and temperature. For deterministic flows we recommend lower temp and beam or constrained decoding when the model variant supports it. Some open models have deterministic decoding modes we can configure in the runtime.
[04:49] Ananya: Any red flags with open models on safety and hallucination for customer-facing outputs?
[04:54] Marcus: There's always risk. We recommend a two-tier approach: use a safety filter + model scoring step and run lower-capacity models for hallucination detection. Redwood Console supports per-route monitoring and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:09] Lena: About compliance: we may need to do a vendor risk assessment. Can you share audit logs format and SAML integration docs?
[05:15] Sofia: Yes; action item — we'll share both. Also include sample contract language we typically see for data processing and residency.
[05:23] Tom: On the engineering side, how easy is switching models? We may want to A/B different open models for cost/quality tradeoffs.
[05:29] Marcus: You can route by policy — latency, cost, region, customer tier — and do canary rollouts, A/B tests. Pin model versions and define automatic fallback to cheaper model variants during load.
[05:41] Ananya: For our initial POC, we want to test three models: Llama-3-70B quantized, Mistral-Base-30B long-context variant, and a multilingual fine-tuned 34B. Preference is to start hosted if we can get accurate perf numbers, then move to Dedicated for scale.
[05:56] Sofia: Sounds sensible. We'll prepare a pricing delta (hosted vs dedicated) and estimated monthly cost for your expected QPS and token volumes.
[06:04] Lena: Also need to know where model weights are stored in hosted — are they in Redwood-managed buckets? And for private deployment, do we need to bring our own model weights?
[06:12] Marcus: Hosted model weights are managed by Redwood (for curated open models), with encryption at rest and access controls. Private can run customer-provided weights if needed; we have an onboarding for model artifacts and signer checks.
[06:24] Ananya: What about function calling ergonomics? Do you expose a helper SDK to map tool outputs back into context?
[06:31] Marcus: Yes, SDKs have function-calling helpers and structured output parsers. Also streaming responses to client are supported for progressive rendering.
[06:39] Sofia: Quick usability note: we'll include a short demo recording of the Redwood Console show-casing rollouts, metrics and cost per token breakdown.
[06:47] Tom: Great. Any performance caveats for multilingual tokenization? We saw token inflation in some languages driving up cost.
[06:52] Marcus: Good point — tokenization differs by model. Some multilingual models use SentencePiece with different vocab coverage. We'll include per-lang tokenization multipliers in the benchmark report.
[07:03] Ananya: Timeline: ideally POC start next month, 6-week evaluation, decision by end of Q2. Is that feasible?
[07:10] Sofia: Yes. With pricing and perf numbers in the next week we can schedule a tech-deep-dive and get a POC running in a couple weeks.
[07:17] Lena: We'll need to loop in procurement and legal early — procurement prefers a standard SLAs and a data processing addendum.
[07:23] Sofia: We'll surface typical SLA language and DPA examples.
[07:27] Marcus: To make benchmarks meaningful please share the 1k multilingual prompts and a small sample of anonymized documents. We'll run head-to-heads across the three model families and provide latency, tokens per second, and per-lang accuracy.
[07:40] Ananya: We'll share that. Also want to test tool-calling reliability under concurrency — ticket lookups with 50 concurrent users.
[07:48] Marcus: We'll include concurrency tests in the perf plan.
[07:51] [08:00] Sofia: Recap — Sofia to send pricing and retention options, Marcus to schedule deep-dive and perf bench, Redwood to share SOC2/ISO/KMS docs, Novagrid to send multilingual prompts and tooling scenarios.
[08:10] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:13] Ananya: Thanks. End.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cash" for "KV cache"), filler words included, some speaker labels simplified. Links shared during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/model-catalog (deck), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (security docs), google drive link: https://drive.example.com/novagrid-samples (shared dataset placeholder).
